comments.value: You would have a stronger case if you presented your alternatives.

What would you propose as an alternative?

So far, I have yet to see anybody discriminate or feel discriminated against due to the new ranking system. I've seen people joke about it before, but nobody actually takes it seriously. I just logged off after hanging out in a public world filled with a varying array of rankings and couldn't see anybody brushing anyone else off because their ranking was higher or lower than anybody elses. 

I think that, with most things, only time will tell. We'll see how it looks in another month or so, but I really think we should be giving the new system a solid run before immediately brushing it off as discriminatory.

As much as I like more safety in the game, I think the new user will have a hard time in VRChat. A lot of people that I know, they already block everything (avatars, shaders, etc...) except for known or higher ranks. Also I don't like how the safety default settings block the new users almost completely like they are not supposed to be seen until they rank up.

@{5baf47bc4180c1700664d937|full_name}: I agree with a lot of this. I was a veteran in the beta and trusted now, I've spent a lot of time playing and contributing to the game but if this system were in place when I joined I would probably not be here today imo. I think the trust system is the best bet we have at the moment, but I do agree default values for low tiered users make them basically invisible.

My extended thoughts: Why punish the innocent casual players who did nothing wrong and just want to have fun meeting new people expressing themselves with avatars? Why automatically treat everyone who doesn't fit into the developers algorithm as an "untrusted unwanted nuisance." There's many reasons users may not have high friend counts, many uploads, or 1000's of hours in the game and that doesn't equate to them being an untrustworthy lesser person as people have already started to show in-game. Adding a hierarchy of user worth isn't an effective fix for the problem. And that doesn't even touch on how fun will it be to be a new user and be instantly barred from communicating with a large portion if the community as you are treated as an unwanted nuisance. It's actively hostile against new players and anyone who isn't orange or higher.

Speaking of that, why such granularity of the ranks other than using it as a popularity contest? I don't understand why there wasn't only two ranks: new and user which would have helped fix this entire issue, though the "algorithm" still is not good as is at differentiating problem users and a good players. 

What's to stop greens, oranges, and purples from crashing you or hijacking your screen? New users cant even do that, they can't upload...

My solutions: 
-Get more moderators. Pay, volunteer, whatever. Many services effectively run on volunteer moderation. Give volunteers incentives for their work. Pay senior mods and treat them as managers to make sure your volunteers are not misbehaving. Require documentation of all actions. Add more mod client tools and make them an active visible player in public maps. The harder you make it to abuse the game, the less people will want to do so.

-Global, per individual player, and friend options for: particles, poly limit,  sounds, ect. If you want to be safe, you can still choose to do that. We don't need the rank system to choose who is privileged enough to be seen and heard for you. If someone is acting shifty, you can pre-block their avatar features just like current muting/blocking. That current addition can stay.

-Keep brand new users from uploading for a bit, that's a fair change to ease moderation work on alt accounts.

-Better review for public uploaded content. It is very lax right now. 

-IP checks for alt accounts and 'seal clubbers'. More tools to help moderation determine bogus accounts intent on harm.

-New user only rooms. For the first few hours, you can only join these special new user areas and communicate there, or play in private rooms with friends. This is how most games handle malicious new account abuse.

-If it is truly an epidemic, Just make the game paid for new players... You fund development and weed out trolls.

---
This idea had it's heart in the right place, but I do not feel it is an effective solution to a problem with many other ways of fixing. We should not be segregating users and hurting new players looking to join, it will just accelerate community stagnation and decline. Who wants to start a new game where you are invisibly ghosted, as in, muted and invisible to many players due to you being new?

@{5ac115035624005f3577dd32|full_name}: I feel like there should only really be 3 ranks (excluding the friend rank because it's not really a rank). New User, User, and Trusted. Maybe have new users' avatars visible by default, but have shaders, particles, and animations turned off. For users, have everything off except avatar and shaders, and trusted users have most things on. That way the system would be less confusing and would help people feel as if its less discriminatory. 

I should note though that I haven't been crashed by anyone so far since the safety update. I actually came across someone (a new user) who was complaining about how she used to crash lots of people but can't anymore, so it's definitely working when it comes to safety.

details: Especially for new users. This will only hurt the player base, segregate players, and overall suffocate the community. There are many other avenues to help fight against abuse or many ways to make the current safety system less hostile to casual and new players.
title: Safety System leads to bullying and descrimination of users
